# Transcode Video to DASH (AV1 / VP9)

- Route: `/tools/transcode-to-dash`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `video`
- Slug: `transcode-to-dash`

## Summary

Package any video into a MPEG-DASH bundle with manifest.mpd + per-rendition init/media segments. (Video tools)

## Details

MPEG-DASH is the open adaptive-streaming standard supported by every modern browser. Media Manipulator transcodes your source video into a DASH VOD bundle — manifest.mpd plus per-rendition init.mp4 and .m4s segments — using AV1 (smaller files, best for new web players) or VP9 (broader playback support). Drop the unzipped folder onto any CDN or origin and serve manifest.mpd to clients. Daily limits and file caps depend on the plan; quote them only from the live plan block.
### What it does
- Probes your source with ffprobe and shows resolution, FPS, duration, codec, and audio status.
- Lets you pick which quality rungs to encode and whether to emit AV1 or VP9.
- Auto-detects the best AV1 encoder available (av1_nvenc → libsvtav1 → libaom-av1).
- Generates an MPEG-DASH manifest.mpd referencing each video Representation plus an AAC audio Representation when present.
- Optionally generates WebVTT captions and storyboard scrubber thumbnails.
- Bundles the result into media-manipulator-dash-<codec>-<jobID>.tar.gz with a report.json and README.
- Uploads the tarball to S3 and hands you back a short-lived presigned GET URL.
### How to use it
1. Upload: Direct S3 presigned PUT — your file never goes through the API server.
2. Probe: ffprobe reads resolution, FPS, audio presence, and codec metadata.
3. Pick rungs + codec: Choose AV1 or VP9 and any combination of 360p/480p/720p.
4. Encode: AV1 (svtav1/libaom/nvenc) or libvpx-vp9 at 2-second segments.
5. Package: manifest.mpd + per-rendition init/segments tar.gz’d with report.json and README.
6. Download: Presigned S3 GET URL valid for 30 minutes.
### Technical details
- AV1 encoder selection prefers av1_nvenc (GPU) when available, falling back to libsvtav1, then libaom-av1.
- VP9 uses libvpx-vp9 with row-mt, frame-parallel decoding, and CRF + bitrate guidance.
- DASH variants are emitted with -seg_duration 2 -use_template 1 -use_timeline 0 -single_file 0.
- manifest.mpd declares one AdaptationSet per content type (video + audio when present) with codecs attributes "av01.0.08M.08" / "vp09.00.51.08" / "mp4a.40.2".
- No upscaling: rungs taller than the source resolution are disabled with a tooltip.
### Use cases
- Modern web players: Shaka Player and dash.js consume manifest.mpd natively.
- Bandwidth-sensitive distribution: AV1 gives near-half the bytes of an H.264 HLS package.
- Internal media library: Self-host adaptive video without paying a SaaS streaming platform.
- Quality testing: A/B AV1 vs VP9 encodes side-by-side from the same source.
### FAQ
Q: AV1 or VP9 — which should I pick?
A: AV1 produces smaller files at equivalent quality, but encoding is slower on CPU-only hosts. VP9 has broader playback support and faster encoding. AV1 is the default.
Q: My server says AV1 is unavailable?
A: AV1 needs one of av1_nvenc (NVIDIA GPU), libsvtav1, or libaom-av1 in FFmpeg. Check /api/video-transcode/capabilities for what your install has.
Q: Is audio always AAC?
A: Yes — the DASH audio AdaptationSet currently emits AAC LC at 128 kbps for maximum compatibility regardless of source codec.
Q: Can I serve this manifest cross-origin?
A: Yes, but your CDN/origin needs the right CORS headers on .mpd, init.mp4, and .m4s files. The tarball does not bundle those headers.
Q: How long does the download URL last?
A: Presigned GET URLs are valid for 30 minutes by default. Re-run the transcode if you need a fresh link.
